title: gpu-oom-cuda-driver-mismatch-debug-scratchpad
content:
Scratchpad: GPU OOM + CUDA / driver / cuDNN mismatch debugging

Context:
- Observed intermittent GPU OOMs and strange CUDA errors on staging inference nodes. Symptoms range from clean OOM from PyTorch to driver/library mismatch messages (Invalid driver API version, cuDNN not found) after container churn.
- Node image: docker image nvcr.io/redwood/pytorch:23.11-cuda11.8 (customer staging stack).
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100-40GB (node reported by infra).

Incidents / snippets (chronological):
1) 2025-02-14 09:12 UTC - OOM during a load test (batch size 8 -> 64)
Command: python run_inference.py --model gpt-small --batch 64
Error: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.36 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 37.82 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 2.14 GiB cached)
Stack: File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1201

Notes: Reducing batch to 16 avoided immediate OOM. Suspect fragmentation/caching. Tried torch.cuda.empty_cache() in code; some improvement but still flaky under concurrency.

2) 2025-02-14 11:05 UTC - After node reboot and docker restart, containers started failing with driver errors
Command: docker logs inference-abc
Error snippet: "libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
Follow-up: python check: import torch; print(torch.version.cuda) -> 11.7
But container expects 11.8 libs. nvidia-smi shows Driver Version: 510.85.02

3) 2025-02-14 11:28 UTC - Mismatch / invalid device function errors during startup:
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:313] failed call to cuInit: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
Runtime error: Invalid device function

Commands run (what I've tried locally on node):
- nvidia-smi -q
- nvcc --version
- python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory)"
- ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudnn.so.8 (inside container)
- docker run --gpus all --rm -it --entrypoint=/bin/bash nvcr.io/redwood/pytorch:23.11-cuda11.8

Outputs / observations:
- nvidia-smi: Driver Version: 510.85.02, CUDA Version: 11.6
- nvcc: CUDA 11.8 toolkit installed in container, but host driver reports 510 (11.6).
- torch.version.cuda == 11.7 inside conda env (mismatch between toolkit + torch build).
- ldd on libcudnn shows missing symlinks to /usr/local/nvidia/lib64 (host-provided).

Quick fixes attempted (and results):
- Restarted docker + nvidia-persistenced: temporary recovery for a few jobs, then errors reappeared.
- Rebooted node: helped for a short window but after heavy load errors returned (suspicion: kernel module/driver gets into bad state under driver older/newer mismatch).
- Upgraded host driver to 520.61.05 (via apt + nvidia-driver installer): reduced mismatch logs but some containers now log "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" when using older images.
- Pinned container cudatoolkit to 11.6 to match driver: avoided some errors but performance was worse; also distros require re-bake images.
- Forced environment var TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 -> reduced fragmentation OOM on some runs.
- Added explicit torch.cuda.empty_cache() + gc.collect() between workloads -> mitigated but not root cause.
- Lowered batch sizes and gradient checkpointing -> workaround for throughput tests.

Hypotheses / root-cause candidates:
- Host driver vs container runtime/toolkit mismatch: many containers include their own libcudnn/cudart that assume higher driver API. When driver < runtime requirements we get driver API errors.
- Kernel module mismatch / stale nvidia kernel module after driver upgrade -> some processes still bound to old libs.
- Memory fragmentation with long-lived processes + dynamic CUDA allocations -> leads to OOM despite large free capacity shown (cached vs allocated confusion).
- Docker image or conda env contains cuDNN built against different libcudnn versions and relies on host /usr/local/nvidia symlinks which may be inconsistent across nodes.
- NCCL timeouts / misconfigured SHM / PID namespace causing collective hangs that look like driver errors (seen in other clusters).

Data to collect next time an incident occurs:
- Full output of nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvidia-smi-$(date +%s).log
- python -c 'import torch,sys,os; print(sys.version, torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.device_count()); print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))'
- ldd of libcudart.so and libcudnn.so inside container and on host (capture file paths): ldd $(python -c "import torch; import os; print(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__)+'/lib/libcudart.so')")
- dmesg | egrep -i "nvrm|nvidia|NVRM|gpu|oom|cuda" and /var/log/syslog / journalctl -k for kernel oopses
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version and check module load times
- /var/log/nvidia-installer.log (if driver install attempted)
- docker inspect <container> to see volume mounts for /usr/local/nvidia and LD_LIBRARY_PATH settings

Repro script (minimal) to run on a node to try to reproduce quickly:

#!/bin/bash
set -e
python - <<'PY'
import torch, time
x = torch.randn(64, 1024, 1024, device='cuda')
print('allocated', x.element_size()*x.nelement())
# allocate a bunch then free
for i in range(5):
    t = [torch.randn(32,1024,1024, device='cuda') for _ in range(3)]
    time.sleep(1)
    del t
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
print('done')
PY

This tends to trigger fragmentation/OOM faster than model loads. Run under the same container image used by jobs.

Next steps / action items:
- Infra: schedule a controlled node reboot + driver re-installation to canonical driver version 535 (recommended for CUDA 11.8/11.7 backwards compatibility). Collect module logs pre/post. (Ticket: INFRA-4123)
- Dev: reproduce locally with the minimal script inside exact container + GPU emulation (or on staging A100). Capture ldd outputs and torch.version outputs.
- CI: add a short smoke test after node maintenance that runs the repro script and validates torch.cuda.is_available() and can allocate a 16GB tensor.
- Ops: enforce consistent image policy: either rely on host driver with containers shipped without cudart/cuDNN, or standardize on images that match host driver ABI.
- Short-term: put a pod/node-level limit on concurrent inference workers (reduce parallelism) until we have stable driver/runtime pairing.

Notes to self / hypotheses to revisit later:
- Check if kernel was automatically updated by apt during image push and driver not rebuilt -> module mismatch.
- Investigate whether NVIDIA Fabric Manager or persistence service was disabled after reboot.
- Validate NCCL socket vs IB configuration; some of the failures looked like collectives timing out under heavy load.

Breadcrumbs / quick commands to run on the node when alerted:
- nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvidia.log && dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.log && journalctl -u docker -n 200 > /tmp/docker.log
- python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())" > /tmp/torch-env.txt
- ls -l /usr/local/nvidia /usr/local/cuda || true
- grep -i nvidia /var/log/syslog | tail -n 200 || true

If this doc helps someone else, paste relevant outputs into INFRA-4123 and @Diego @Priya for follow-up.

-- Asha
